description: Environmental Resilience Institute Toolkit (ERIT) is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Indiana University | Environmental Resilience Institute; EPA, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. This interactive resource helps decision makers create an integrated package of information about climate change tailored specifically to their community and their needs. Users select a region of interest, then indicate areas of potential concern. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Air Quality, Changing Seasons, Drought, Extreme Cold, Extreme Heat, Flooding – General, Shifting Species, Habitats, and Ecosystems, Vector-Borne Disease, Water Quality. Assets: Agriculture and Food Supply, Critical Facilities, Energy and Utilities, Forestry, Natural Areas and Wildlife, Property, Transportation and Mobility, Urban Landscape and Tree Canopy, Water Infrastructure – General. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
